title: Man. Post. Cap. X: GAR — Mosaic rites point to Christ; the primal ceremony did not
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles: do not grant the chain that legal ceremonies are abrogated, that this ban was ceremonial, and therefore abrogated. When legal ceremonies are named here they mean without doubt the ritual statutes God set for Israel by Moses—commonly Mosaic ceremonies. That Christ’s coming abrogated them is no wonder: they were shadows and figures whose truth and body is in Christ (Col 2:17), all looking to him as their complement. But the ceremony inside this primitive law did not look to Christ as its significate. So it does not follow that antiquating those Israelite rites by that fact also abrogates the primordial law so that it has no further use and in no way looks to humans.
pass_b_english: GAR. Meanwhile it is not to be thought that that argumentation is legitimate: that the legal ceremonies have been abrogated; that this is a ceremonial law; and so abrogated and abolished.

For legal ceremonies, when they are named here, are without doubt understood as those ritual or ceremonial statutes which God constituted for Israel by the hand of Moses; whence they are also commonly called Mosaic ceremonies.
That they were abrogated at Christ’s coming is no wonder, since they were shadows and figures whose truth and body is in Christ (Colossians 2:17).
For they all looked to Christ as to their complement.
But the ceremony which was in this primitive law did not look to Christ as to its significate.

Hence it does not follow that if those Israelite ceremonies have been antiquated, it must be concluded by that very fact that that primordial law has also been abrogated, so that there is no longer any use of it, and it in no way looks to humans.
source_text: GAR. Interim non est quod putemus legitimam esse illam argumentationem: legales ceremonias esse abrogatas; hanc esse legem ceremonialem; itaque abrogatam abolitamque. Nam legales ceremoniae, cum hic nominantur, sine dubitatione intelliguntur statuta illa ritualia sive ceremonalia, quae sunt a Deo Israeli constituta per manum Mosis; unde & ceremoniae Mosaicae vulgo dicuntur. Eas Christi adventu abrogatas fuisse nihil mirum est, cum umbrae essent & figurae quarum veritas & corpus est in Christo, Coloss. 2. 17. Respiciebant enim omnes ad Christum tanquam ad complementum suum. At ceremonia, quae in hac primitiva lege inerat, ad Christum non respiciebat tanquam ad significatum suum. Unde non consequitur, ut si ceremoniae illae Israeliticae antiquatae sunt, concludendum sit eo ipso, etiam abrogatam esse legem illam primordialem, ita ut nullus sit amplius eius usus, & ad homines nulla ratione spectet.
